AUDITED CLAIM AND INTERFACE

Input rational a,c>=0, binary integer n>=0, and p>=1. For nonzero
H_n=[x^n] exp(a*x^2/2+c*x), return a logarithmic interval of width at most
2^(-p-1), or a floating enclosure with binary-encoded exponent. Exact zeros
are reported separately. This interface is essential: an expanded exact
rational H_n can have exponentially many output bits in bitlength(n).

I found no mathematical counterexample to deterministic bit-polynomial
evaluation under this interface. Below are independent reconstructions of
the uniform bounds, an explicit alternative interpolation algorithm that
removes a Taylor-conditioning gap, and precise software evidence.

1. IDENTITY, PARITY, AND EXTREME PARAMETERS

For a,c>0 put d=c/sqrt(a), sigma=(-1)^n, b(t)=1+sigma*exp(-2dt),
m=(d+sqrt(d*d+4n))/2, and phi(t)=n*log(t)-(t-d)^2/2.
The Gaussian moment identity gives
 H_n=a^(n/2)/(n!*sqrt(2*pi))*integral_0^infinity exp(phi(t))*b(t) dt.
No additional exp(-d*d/2) factor is missing. Splitting the signed Gaussian
moment into positive and negative half-lines yields exactly this formula.

Set F(m+s)=exp(phi(m+s)-phi(m))*b(m+s)/b(m). Then
 log H_n=(n/2)log(a)-logGamma(n+1)-.5log(2*pi)
          +n log(m)-.5(n/m)^2+log b(m)+log I,
 I=integral_0^infinity F(t)dt.
The identity m-d=n/m is crucial; computing m-d by subtraction would be an
unnecessary numerical vulnerability when d is large.

For odd n, b is increasing, concave, vanishes at zero, and is positive for
t>0. Hence min(1,t/m)<=b(t)/b(m)<=max(1,t/m). Moreover for z=t+iy,t>0,
 b(z)=2dz integral_0^1 exp(-2dzv)dv,
 |b(z)|<=|z|*b(t)/t.
This cancels the common small displacement analytically. There is no
inverse-tiny-displacement blowup in the normalized complex integrand.
For even n, 1/2<=b(t)/b(m)<=2 and |b(z)/b(m)|<=2 when Re(z)>0.

If the rational inputs have total binary length L, nonzero d is at least
2^(-O(L)); b(m)>=min(d*m,1/2)>=2^(-O(L)), because m>=1. Thus even a direct
division by a rigorously enclosed odd b(m) costs only O(L) extra bits.
Use expm1 or cancel d when evaluating that factor.

2. REAL LOWER BOUND AND TAILS

phi'(m)=0 and phi''(t)=-1-n/t^2<=-1, so F's exponential factor is at most
exp(-s*s/2). For t in [m,m+1], n/t^2<=1, giving the lower bound exp(-s*s).
The parity factor is at least 1/2 there. Consequently
 I >= .5 integral_0^1 exp(-s*s)ds >= .5 integral_0^1(1-s*s)ds = 1/3.

source_excerpts.text:
TASK AND OUTPUT INTERFACE

For rational a,c>=0, binary integer n>=0 and p>=1, evaluate
  H_n=[x^n] exp(a*x^2/2+c*x)
with relative error <=2^-p. The intended output is a certified logarithmic
interval, or a binary floating enclosure with a binary-encoded exponent.
For the logarithmic interface require interval width <=2^-(p+1); choosing
any point in that interval and exponentiating then gives relative error
at most exp(2^-(p+1))-1<=2^-p.
An ordinary exact rational expansion may require Omega(n) output bits and
is NOT the promised interface. Let B=bitlength(n) and L be the input bit
length of a,c. This note constructs an arithmetic procedure polynomial in
B+L+p. It does not claim that an existing special-function implementation
automatically has this complexity.

The positive real integral below removes the tiny-displacement parity
cancellation. A two-saddle local CLT is not necessary.

1. EXACT POSITIVE INTEGRAL

Assume a,c>0 and n>=1. Put d=c/sqrt(a), s=(-1)^n, and
  b_s(t)=1+s*exp(-2*d*t),
  m=(d+sqrt(d^2+4*n))/2.
Then m>=sqrt(n)>=1 and m-d=n/m. Gaussian moments give
  H_n = a^(n/2)/(n!*sqrt(2*pi))
        * integral_0^infty t^n exp(-(t-d)^2/2) b_s(t) dt.
For even n the integrand is a positive sum. For odd n it is a positive
difference; evaluate b_-(t) as -expm1(-2*d*t), or analytically strip d.

Define the entire function (n is an integer)
  F(z)=(z/m)^n
       * exp[-n*(z-m)/m-(z-m)^2/2]
       * b_s(z)/b_s(m),
and I=integral_0^infty F(t) dt. Exactly,
  H_n = a^(n/2) m^n exp[-(n/m)^2/2]
        * b_s(m) I / (n!*sqrt(2*pi)).                 (1)
The corresponding log expression avoids huge intermediate powers.

Special cases: H_0=1; a=0 gives c^n/n!; c=0 gives zero for odd n and
(a/2)^(n/2)/(n/2)! for even n. With a=c=0 and n>0 the result is zero.

2. REAL BOUNDS UNIFORM IN d

Set phi(t)=n*log(t)-(t-d)^2/2. Then phi'(m)=0 and
  phi''(t)=-1-n/t^2<=-1.
Thus for x=t-m with t>0,
  exp(phi(t)-phi(m)) <= exp(-x^2/2).                 (2)
On t in [m,m+1], n/t^2<=1, so phi(t)-phi(m)>=-(t-m)^2.

For even n, 1/2 <= b_+(t)/b_+(m) <=2 for all t>0.
For odd n, b_-(t) is positive, increasing, concave, and zero at t=0.
Consequently
  min(1,t/m) <= b_-(t)/b_-(m) <=max(1,t/m).         (3)
It follows that
  I >= (1/2)*integral_0^1 exp(-x^2) dx
    >=1/(2*e)>1/6.                                (4)

For R>=1, the omitted integral outside |t-m|<=R is at most
  4*exp(-R^2/2).

source_excerpts.text:
DISPLACED ONE-HERALD FOLLOWUP — CONSTRUCTIVE COEFFICIENT EVALUATION
Date: 10 October 2026. Supplemental branch, frozen v2 code unchanged.
Status: internally reconstructed proof and completed supplemental sampler; independent model audits completed. Authoritative endpoint review: ../gaussian_software_audit/displaced/report.txt. Coefficient proof review: ../gaussian_displaced_audit/report.txt. No external/formal verification or historical novelty claim. The earlier displaced_gate.txt accurately refuted a naive single-unimodal-envelope route; it is superseded as a claim that no constructive route is available.

THE DECISIVE CHANGE
A two-saddle Fourier local-CLT approximation is unnecessary. Fold the real Gaussian moment integral onto the positive half-line. This combines the parity-related saddles before numerical approximation and leaves a positive integrand, including arbitrarily small displacement at odd n. Its normalized width and complex analyticity bounds are uniform in the coefficient order and displacement.

COEFFICIENT THEOREM
Let a,c>=0 be rational, n>=0 an integer encoded in binary, and p>=1. Write H_n=[z^n]exp(a z^2/2+c z). There is a deterministic algorithm polynomial in total coefficient input length L, log(n+1), and p which either recognizes H_n=0 or produces an enclosure of log H_n of absolute width<=2^(-p). Equivalently one obtains a relative-accuracy enclosure in floating mantissa/exponent representation. Exact rational H_n is not the output: its numerator/denominator may require Omega(n) bits.
Zero/elementary cases: H_0=1; a=0 gives c^n/n!; c=0 gives H_even=(a/2)^(n/2)/(n/2)! and H_odd=0; a=c=0 handled directly.

POSITIVE INTEGRAL IDENTITY
For a,c>0, set d=c/sqrt(a), s=(-1)^n and m=(d+sqrt(d^2+4n))/2. Then m>=sqrt(n), m>=d and m-d=n/m. Since n!H_n is the n-th moment of N(c,a),
 H_n = a^(n/2)/(n!sqrt(2pi)) integral_0^infty t^n exp[-(t-d)^2/2] b_s(t) dt,
 b_s(t)=1+s exp(-2dt).
For even n the bracket is positive and >=1. For odd n it is positive for t>0 and equals -expm1(-2dt). There is no subtraction of two large integrated quantities.
Normalize at m:
 G(t)=exp{n[log(t/m)-(t-m)/m]-(t-m)^2/2} b_s(t)/b_s(m),
 I=integral_0^infty G(t)dt.
The prefactor can be evaluated stably in logarithms:
 log H_n=(n/2)log a-logGamma(n+1)-(1/2)log(2pi)+n log m
          -(1/2)(n/m)^2+log b_s(m)+log I.
Using m-d=n/m avoids subtracting close large numbers.

UNIFORM
